annotations.title: Create an upload URL for a file

description: Get a URL for one file up to 15 MB, with its `name` and `type`. You need a shell that can reach our API: PUT the raw bytes to the URL with no API key header, outside MCP, for example `curl -T invoice.pdf <url>`. The URL works once, for 15 minutes. Keep it secret. The PUT answers the stored file, with its `id` and `sha256`. A retry of a used URL that still works answers the same file without reading the bytes again. We check that the key and the person who made it still have permission before reading the bytes and again before storing them, retries included. An Idempotency-Key replay of this call has url null: if the first answer was lost, call again with a new Idempotency-Key. The workspace keeps up to 1,024 MB of files in all, counting 15 MB for each upload URL not used yet; past that it answers 409 serverErrors.fileStorageFull. A file is kept while an unsent draft or a scheduled, reserved or sending email uses it, and deleted 7 days after it was stored or last used, or sooner with delete_file (409 serverErrors.filePinned while in use); reading or listing it doesn't change that. Attach up to 10 files by passing their ids as fileIds to create_draft, update_draft, draft_reply, reply_to_message or send_transactional_message.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

name.description: The file's name, like invoice-1042.pdf, up to 255 characters. We take out control and invisible characters, slashes and double quotes, and keep the rest as you wrote it.

type.description: The file's type, like application/pdf or image/png. Left out, application/octet-stream. We keep what you say and never read the bytes to check it.
